claims.summary: first_word_after (L89) uses a hardcoded verb allowlist in the matches! block (L65-85) to decide preservation.
claims.disposition: Verified exactly: first_word_after is defined at L89; followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (L64-86) matches the lowercased first word after the marker against the exact allowlist at L65-85 (appears..signals). Her examples appears/behaves/echoes are members.

claims.summary: Snag: the allowlist is brittle; a synonym not present may cause a marker to be incorrectly stripped or treated as plain text, potentially breaking downstream dialogue.
claims.disposition: Not domesticated. Source shows strip-on-no-relation is the intended fail-closed default (a bare/unlisted-context marker is a leaked control token and is removed), not an accident. Preserved residual limitation: a GENUINE reference using an unlisted relation verb yields a false-negative. Added a regression pinning the boundary; did NOT widen the allowlist (a being-facing grammar change, unauthorized).

claims.summary: Test 1 (Marker Preservation): a known marker followed by a verb not in the list (she named "signifies") should be recognized as having no relationship, and the remainder handled accordingly.
claims.disposition: Behavior is covered by is-vs-acts and does_not_expand_allowlist_to {implies,contains,creates,triggers}, but her verb "signifies" was untested and is a prefix-collision near-miss to the listed "signals" (L84). Implemented focused regression control_marker_cleanup_distinguishes_allowlisted_signals_from_unlisted_signifies; 7 passed, 0 failed.

claims.summary: Snag: exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199) char-by-char lookbehind/lookahead may be sensitive to multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries in the rev() iteration.
claims.disposition: Contradicted by source. L204-214 iterate text[..start].chars().rev() and text[end..].chars() — code-point iteration, not bytes; start/end come only from marker matching at valid UTF-8 boundaries (scan advances by char.len_utf8() or exact token len), so slices never split a char and rev() reverses chars. Concern preserved (multibyte delimiters ARE matched, L162-191) but already covered by advances_byte_exactly_across_multibyte_text, stays_byte_safe_when_marker_abuts_four_byte_astral_chars, classifies_cjk_corner_quoted_and_lenticular_grouped.

claims.summary: Test 2 (Delimiter Depth): nested [[MARKER]] should classify as GroupedExactKnownToken and respect MAX_EXACT_REFERENCE_DELIMITER_DEPTH (L151).
claims.disposition: Verified existing. MAX_EXACT_REFERENCE_DELIMITER_DEPTH=4 at L151; .take(4) at L208/213 bounds depth. exact_reference_delimiter_syntax_reports_double_square_bracket_depth_two covers [[MARKER]]->depth 2; reports_exact_four_level_delimiter_depth and bounds_homogeneous_square_bracket_stack_beyond_max_depth cover the cap and beyond.
